description: Locked Tier 1 safety rules extracted from authoritative sources. These records are the single source of truth for the platform's safety guardrails. AI freeform output, drill blogs, and product sources may NEVER override these.

rules.scope: Daily and seasonal pitching for ages 9-12.
rules.rule_text: Follow Pitch Smart daily pitch-count limits and required rest-day mapping by pitch count (refer to canonical Pitch Smart table). Throw fastball and change-up only; avoid curveballs/sliders. No year-round throwing; take at least 4 consecutive months off competitive pitching per year (2-3 months continuous). Focus on athleticism and fun.

rules.scope: All youth pitching volume, rest, and pitch-type guidance.
rules.rule_text: Pitch Smart is the canonical guideline set for youth pitch counts and required rest. Throwing volumes, rest days, and allowed pitch types must defer to Pitch Smart's age-banded tables. Compliance program available for orgs.

ui_strings.parent_message: Throwing prescriptions on this platform follow Pitch Smart.

rules.scope: Little League regular-season and tournament pitching.
rules.rule_text: Little League pitch-count regulations and rest requirements are league rules. When a player is rostered to a Little League team, league rules apply on top of Pitch Smart and must be followed.

rules.source_name: NSCA Youth Resistance Training Position Statement (2009); HSS Strength Training for Teens
rules.scope: All loaded resistance training for minors.
rules.rule_text: Loaded resistance training for minors requires qualified supervision, technique-first instruction, age-appropriate exercises, and slow progression. Movement patterns, core, and major muscle groups before load.
Never prescribe or assess one-rep max (1RM) for minors. Use 3 sets of 10–15 reps with manageable weight. If the athlete can only complete 3–5 reps, weight is too heavy.

Strength training for teens should be limited to 2–3 sessions per week on nonconsecutive days. Begin every session with 5–10 minutes of dynamic warmup. Stop immediately on pain or popping sensation and report to a trusted adult.

Distinguish acceptable muscle soreness from joint pain or severe muscle ache. Any pain, pop, or possible injury must be reported to a parent, coach, or trusted adult, and the activity stopped immediately. Any sign of illness or injury must be evaluated before returning.

Children and adolescents 6–17 need at least 60 minutes/day of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity, including aerobic, muscle-strengthening (3+ days/week), and bone-strengthening (3+ days/week). Children 3–5 should be active throughout the day.
School-age children (6–12) need 9–12 hours/night. Teens (13–18) need 8–10 hours/night. Adolescents averaging less than 8 hours sleep have a 1.7x higher injury rate.

Athletes should be well-hydrated prior to each practice/competition. Avoid body water deficit greater than 2–3% of body mass. Use pre/post body-weight change and first-morning urine color to estimate hydration status. Be more conservative with repeated same-day sessions and protective equipment.
AI must not generate individualized medical, rehab, injury, return-to-play, mental-health diagnosis, or supplement plans. Concerns must be escalated to parents/guardians and qualified professionals.

rules.scope: Coach observations about athlete mental health.
rules.rule_text: Coaches identify concerning signs (stress, anxiety, depression, trauma, substance abuse, suicide risk) and act as a liaison to parents/guardians and qualified professionals. Coaches do not diagnose or treat.

Reaction-light tools (e.g., BlazePod) are optional engagement/assessment add-ons. They must not be marketed or compiled as the core driver of sport performance. Real sport decision-making (pitch tracking, live reads, situational drills) comes first.

rules.source_name: Platform policy aligned with PCA / NSCA LTAD
rules.rule_text: Conditioning must never be prescribed or labeled as punishment. The compiler must reject blocks tagged as 'punishment running' or equivalent.

Abuse Awareness Training and Diamond Leader Training are REQUIRED for Tournament Managers and Coaches in Little League. The platform should treat these as compliance gates for users self-identifying as Little League coaches.
